clue.text: Suggest bet should exclude new member of rugby team

indicators.note: to exclude something is to leave it out, so this letter is dropped from the bet

parts.note: to punt is to bet
a forward is one of the pack in a rugby team

explanation.surface: A rugby punter is told to back the team but leave out the latest signing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should exclude' takes N out of PUNT, leaving PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward an idea or name is to propose it, a synonym of suggest.

clue.text: Crown put away under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue the eating word sits below the letter for pressure

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
to put away food is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: A crown jewel is stowed away under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown of the head is its top, also known by this old word.

clue.text: Criticise drink and criticise paintings etc

parts.note: tea is a drink
to rap is to criticise sharply
art covers paintings and similar works

explanation.surface: A critic slates the refreshments and also the pictures at an exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull something to pieces in a review is to attack it fiercely, a synonym of criticise.

clue.text: A theatre, set up in support of ordinary theatrical production

indicators.note: in a down clue the support goes underneath, so the reversed letters sit beneath the letter for ordinary
in a down clue set up means written upwards, reversing the letters

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre

explanation.surface: A theatre is founded to back an everyday stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns AREP into PERA, which 'in support of' places below O.
explanation.definitionFit: A staged drama set to music is a kind of theatrical production.

clue.text: Substantial crew entering river, expending energy

indicators.note: to expend energy is to use it up, so that letter is lost
the crew goes into the river's name

parts.note: the Wye is a river on the England-Wales border
an eight is a rowing crew
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A sturdy rowing crew launches into a river and uses up its strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' gives WEIGHTYE; 'expending' drops an E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heavy or important carries weight, so is of considerable size or significance.

clue.text: Function absorbed by meet

parts.note: to run is to function, as a machine does
to be into something is to be keen on or absorbed by it

explanation.surface: A function soaked up by a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To come across someone by chance is to encounter them, to meet.

clue.text: I advanced in company? This is more of a dismissal

definitions.text: This is more of a dismissal

indicators.note: the letters for I and advanced are placed inside the abbreviation for company

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: Someone moving up in a firm wonders if a farewell, rather than promotion, is on the cards.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'advanced': a greeting that sends someone on their way is a parting word rather than a welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian word is a casual goodbye, so it serves to send someone off.

clue.text: Chancing to overlook top location for birthday message?

indicators.note: overlooking the top means leaving out the first letter in a down clue

parts.note: dicing, as in dicing with death, means taking chances

explanation.surface: Someone takes a gamble and skips the top line of a birthday card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chancing' gives DICING, as in dicing with death; dropping its first letter leaves the answer. The question mark flags that a cake's topping is only one place for a message.
explanation.definitionFit: Birthday greetings are often piped on to the sugary coating of a cake.

clue.text: Inspiring invention for when the pressure's off?

definitions.text: Inspiring invention for when the pressure's off?

parts.words: Inspiring invention for when the pressure's off?
parts.note: inspiring is literal, breathing in, and the pressure is cabin pressure lost in an aircraft, not stress

explanation.surface: A clever creation that motivates people once stress has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests relaxing; in fact an aircraft has lost cabin pressure and something must help passengers breathe.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathing apparatus drops from an aircraft ceiling when cabin pressure fails.

clue.text: Love story mostly about love in Paris (Eastern)

indicators.note: about means these letters go round the French word

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: a tale is a story
rien is French for nothing, and nothing is love in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A romance set largely around love in Paris, with an Eastern note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' appears twice: once as O, the tennis zero, and once in French as nothing; 'mostly' cuts the last letter of the story and 'about' wraps the pair round the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental describes things from Asia, the East.

clue.text: Hurry to reverse European traffic

indicators.note: to reverse something is to turn it backwards, so the hurry word is read right to left

parts.note: to dart is to hurry

explanation.surface: A driver is told to speed up while backing out of European traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' looks like cars on a road but is a noun for commerce; 'to reverse' reads the hurry word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic as a noun means commerce or dealing in goods, as in drug traffic.

clue.text: Urban area, part of target unknown movement backed

parts.note: the inner is the ring of an archery target next to the bull

indicators.note: backed means the letters are put in back-to-front order

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown
a tic is an involuntary movement

explanation.surface: An archer's target area and some mysterious twitch are both supported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns YTIC into CITY.
explanation.definitionFit: The central part of a large town, often deprived, is a built-up district of a city.

clue.text: Arab blocking American subject running race

indicators.note: to block a passage is to sit in it, so these letters sit inside the subject

parts.note: math is the American name for the school subject mathematics
Ar. is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: An Arab gets in the way of an American who is the subject of a running race.
explanation.walkthrough: Americans say math where Britons say maths; 'blocking' sets the Arabic abbreviation in the middle of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-distance footrace of about 26 miles is one well-known kind of race.

clue.text: Almost hungry, having bagged large bird

indicators.note: to bag something is to capture it, so the letter goes inside
almost means the word is not quite complete, so its last letter is missing

parts.note: eager can mean hungry, keen for something

explanation.surface: A greedy creature has caught a big bird to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts EAGER to EAGE; 'having bagged' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bird of prey with a hooked beak is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Result of visitors from afar giving you a ring on the farm?

definitions.text: Result of visitors from afar giving you a ring on the farm?

parts.words: Result of visitors from afar giving you a ring on the farm?
parts.note: the visitors are aliens supposedly landing, and the ring is a flattened pattern in a field of wheat, not a phone call

explanation.surface: Guests from far away phone you at the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving you a ring' reads as phoning; it is a literal ring left in a field, popularly blamed on extraterrestrials.
explanation.definitionFit: Mysterious flattened rings in cornfields are often jokingly blamed on alien landings.

clue.text: Monarch's state? Not good, it's true

indicators.note: not here means without, so the letter for good is left out

parts.note: regality is the condition of being royal, a monarch's status

explanation.surface: Someone muses that the condition of being a king is no good, and that is a fact.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing G from REGALITY leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is a fact rather than an illusion is actual, which is what the phrase describes.

clue.text: Suggestion pub venture's ending in ruin

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: that final letter goes inside the ruin word

parts.note: to undo someone is to ruin them

indicators.note: ending means just the final letter of the venture word

explanation.surface: A pub business ends up ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' takes E from venture's, which 'in' puts inside UNDO.
explanation.definitionFit: An insinuation is an indirect, often suggestive, remark.

clue.text: I'm engaged in work with corporation — most favourable outcome

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: to be engaged in something is to be inside it, so these letters go within

parts.note: corporation is an old jocular word for a pot belly, a tum
I'm without the apostrophe gives IM

explanation.surface: Someone working with a large company reckons it will end up as the best possible result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' reads as a business but is old British slang for a pot belly; 'engaged in' places I'M within it.
explanation.definitionFit: The optimum is the best or most favourable result achievable.

clue.text: Scar military officer's put on sweet overseas trader

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces sit on top of the sweet

parts.note: to mar is to scar or spoil
CO is a commanding officer
Polo is a British brand of mint sweet with a hole

explanation.surface: A soldier's scar is blamed on a sweet bought abroad by a trader.
explanation.walkthrough: Polo is a ring-shaped British peppermint.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian merchant who travelled to China is a famous trader from overseas.

clue.text: Given a hint about turning up with classic sidekick?

indicators.note: turning means the little word is spun round end to end

parts.note: Tonto was the Lone Ranger's companion in the classic Western series

explanation.surface: Someone was tipped off about a sidekick from the classics making a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: Tonto is the Lone Ranger's companion in the old American radio and TV Western; 'turning' flips the little word before him.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put onto something is to be directed towards it or tipped off about it.

clue.text: Small item included in examination dealing with planetary motion

indicators.note: to be included in something is to be inside it

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam
a bit is a small piece

explanation.surface: A small question features in an astronomy exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Planets travel in orbits, so their motion is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Certain British back besieging the French country

indicators.note: to besiege is to surround, so the reversed letters go round the French article
back means the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: sure means certain
la is the feminine form of the in French

explanation.surface: A confident Brit backs an assault on the French nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SUREB into BERUS, which 'besieging' splits around LA.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Soviet republic in eastern Europe is one example of a country.

clue.text: Sense of shame, heading off into bar erected with other shops and houses?

indicators.note: the trimmed shame word goes into the reversed bar
in a down clue erected means built upwards, so reversed

parts.note: a pub is a bar

indicators.note: heading off means its first letter is lost

parts.note: guilt is a sense of shame

explanation.surface: A guilty feeling goes into a bar newly put up among shops and homes.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'erected' means written upwards; 'heading off' drops the first letter of the shame word, and 'into' sets it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A densely developed district is covered with buildings, such as homes and shops.

clue.text: Peter out after getting elected for production company

indicators.note: the letters for peter out come after those for elected

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in
to die away is to peter out

explanation.surface: A man called Peter leaves after winning an election and heads a production firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like a name, but 'Peter out' is the verb, to fade away.
explanation.definitionFit: An independent record label or film studio, outside the major corporations, is called by this short name.

clue.text: The necessary expression of disgust after party

indicators.note: the disgusted cry comes after the party word

parts.note: a do is a party
ugh is a cry of disgust

explanation.surface: Someone groans in disgust at the cost after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the necessary' is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough and the necessary are both slang for cash.

clue.text: Bishop moving with the times in resort

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
right-on describes someone fashionable or up to date

explanation.surface: A progressive churchman modernising at a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON is a seaside resort on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The south-coast town is a famous seaside holiday destination, an example of a resort.

clue.text: Son leaving beach, perhaps, shepherding daughter in crowd

indicators.note: a shepherd herds sheep, surrounding them, so the letter goes inside
the letter for son leaves, dropping out of the beach word

parts.note: a beach is one kind of shore

explanation.surface: A son leaves the seaside while minding his daughter in the crush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes S from SHORE, giving HORE; 'shepherding' puts D inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a large gathering of people, a mob.

clue.text: Aggrieved feelings about a source of fuel

indicators.note: about means the sulk word goes round the letter

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulky resentment, as in in a pet

explanation.surface: Resentment over a fuel supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried turf from bogs is burned as a fuel.

clue.text: Subversive activity ended by detective in film

indicators.note: the letters for ended and detective are put inside the film word

parts.note: a coat is a thin film or layer, as of paint
when time is up it has ended

explanation.surface: A film about subversives ends with a detective case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' suggests a movie but means a layer, COAT, with UPDET inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden illegal seizure of power from a government is subversion in action.

clue.text: River runs north through garden

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: the letter for north runs through the middle of the garden word

parts.note: to hoe is to work a garden

explanation.surface: A river flows northwards through a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'garden' is a verb here, HOE, with N inside giving HONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The great waterway of Switzerland and south-east France is an example of a river.

clue.text: Tail removed from genuine old parrot

indicators.note: losing the tail means dropping the final letter of the word for genuine

parts.note: echt, borrowed from German, means genuine

explanation.surface: A genuine old parrot has had its tail feathers pulled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parrot' is a verb, to repeat; ECHT loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat what someone says mechanically is to mimic or parrot them.

clue.text: Decrepit, but given a rousing send-off

definitions.meaning: worn out and broken down, as an old car might be

explanation.surface: An old wreck that nonetheless got a warm farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapped-out is slang for worn out, and someone cheered as they leave was applauded away.
